investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official '/programmation/' page — found only a client-hydrated Nuxt 3 shell with no event data in the static HTML. Level 2 STRUCTURAL: the same retained page's own <script data-src="/programmation/_payload.json?..."> tag publicly references this SPA's own build-time data endpoint; a further plain GET (no query string needed) against that endpoint returned this venue's full, real event list (114 records) as a Nuxt/devalue-encoded JSON payload.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://www.bataclan.fr/programmation/ returned a 280,251-byte Nuxt 3 SSR shell. Its own inline <script id="__NUXT_DATA__"> block decodes to only app/UI state (locale, scroll position, modal flags) — no event records at all. No JSON-LD, ICS, or WordPress/Events-Calendar signal was found anywhere on the page.

The same retained page's own markup carries <script type="application/json" data-nuxt-data="nuxt-app" data-ssr="true" id="__NUXT_DATA__" data-src="/programmation/_payload.json?...">, a publicly referenced (not private/undocumented) Nuxt build data endpoint. A plain GET of that same path (confirmed to also work without its query-string build hash) returned a 929,421-byte JSON body containing this venue's full, real 114-event schedule with title/date/venue/price/ticketing-url per event. This fully answered the investigation question; no further escalation was needed.

venue_reference: Le Bataclan (concert hall, 50 Boulevard Voltaire, 75011 Paris)

identity.notes: The retained page's own <title> reads 'La programmation | Bataclan - Bataclan' at the venue's own domain bataclan.fr. The same retained page's own footer states the venue's own address directly: '50 Boulevard Voltaire' / '75011 Paris' — matching the assigned venue address exactly.

site_classification.platform: Nuxt 3 (SSR/hydrated SPA), custom back-office (CMS record ids/uids resembling Strapi), ticketing via a first-party 'billetterie.bataclan.fr' subdomain ('Hubber'-style checkout, referenced directly on each record's own ticketingUrl). The static HTML shell carries no event data itself, but publicly references a static, discoverable '_payload.json' data endpoint that does.

title.notes: Each decoded record's own 'attributes.title', stated directly.

start_date.notes: Each decoded record's own 'attributes.date' is a full ISO-8601 UTC instant (e.g. '2026-09-15T17:00:00.000Z'), stated directly. Cross-checked against this same record's own free-text description ('mardi 15 septembre 2026' / '19h' cross-training start) — 17:00 UTC = 19:00 Europe/Paris (CEST, UTC+2) in September, consistent.

time.value: 17:00:00Z (= 19:00 Europe/Paris local, CEST) — a genuine UTC instant, not merely a floating local time
time.notes: The same 'attributes.date' field directly carries a full UTC instant with an explicit 'Z' suffix on every sampled record — not a floating local time requiring separate timezone resolution.

end.notes: A parallel 'attributes.dateEnd' field is present but was found — by sampling across the retained 114-record dataset — to be identical to 'attributes.date' for 107 of 114 records and to differ for only 7, with no retained evidence proving what that difference represents (a true performance end-time vs. some other CMS bookkeeping field, as previously found for Tempodrom Berlin's own analogous 'endDate' field — see research/source-investigations/tempodrom-berlin-01/). Honestly recorded NOT_PRESENT rather than promoted to a claimed performance end-time.

venue_location.notes: This is a single-venue source. Each record's own 'attributes.meetings[].venue' field directly states 'Bataclan' (confirmed identical across every sampled record); the retained page's own footer directly states the full address.

source_record_id.notes: Each record's own 'id' field is this source's own CMS record primary key, directly exposed on every record (not a derived/guessed value) — the same class of documented, source-owned identifier already accepted for other WordPress-post-ID- and CMS-record-ID-based sources in this project (e.g. ingestion/badehaus/, ingestion/zenner/).

event_url.notes: Each record's own 'attributes.ticketingUrl' field, stated directly. This is a first-party subdomain of the venue's own official domain (billetterie.bataclan.fr under bataclan.fr) — not a third-party aggregator.

price.notes: Each record's own first 'attributes.meetings[0].price_min'/'price_max' fields are stated directly as plain decimal numbers. Currency (EUR) is not a separate dedicated field on this record, but is corroborated directly by this SAME record's own free-text 'description' field, which repeats the identical numeric amounts immediately next to a '€' symbol (e.g. 'Prix unique ... : 39 €', '... : 78 €') — a genuine corroboration within one record, not a separate contextual combination, so recorded as DIRECT_SOURCE rather than DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT.

recommended_family NEW_FAMILY_REQUIRED — this Nuxt-payload acquisition shape (list-page shell + publicly-referenced devalue-encoded data endpoint) does not match any existing COLLECTOR_FAMILIES member. The low-level devalue-array index-resolution step itself reuses the EXISTING, unmodified ingestion/sveltekit-data/decode.mjs resolveDevalueRef() primitive (already proven generic/source-agnostic); only the Nuxt-specific envelope navigation and field-mapping (ingestion/le-bataclan/) are new, bespoke code.
